title: Remap a shortcut is not working when targeting git-bash

status.label: Fix process targeting for Git Bash shortcuts
status.detail: A user reproduced the Shift+A-to-B failure on PowerToys 0.100.2; targeting mintty.exe works, while targeting git-bash.exe does not identify its child terminal process.

judgment.rationale: The reporter says a Shift+A-to-B remap targeting git-bash.exe sends uppercase A, while the same mapping works in Chrome and when targeting all apps. A later commenter reproduced the problem on PowerToys 0.100.2 and reports that targeting mintty.exe works because PowerToys does not recognize mintty as a child of git-bash.exe. This current reproduction narrows the defect to process targeting for the Git Bash terminal child rather than a general shortcut failure.
evidence: The original report lists PowerToys 0.81.1 and a Shift+A-to-B shortcut targeting git-bash.exe, which produces A instead of b.
The reporter says the mapping works when targeting chrome.exe or All apps.
A commenter reproduced on PowerToys 0.100.2 with Git 2.53.0.2 and Windows 11 25H2.
The current-build commenter says targeting mintty.exe works, but PowerToys does not identify mintty as a child of git-bash.exe.
judgment.recommended_action: Correct or extend Keyboard Manager process targeting so shortcuts configured for git-bash.exe also apply to its mintty terminal child, while preserving app-specific targeting.

fix_assessment.rationale: A current-build reproduction and a working mintty.exe workaround isolate the failure to parent/child process identity resolution for Git Bash shortcut remaps.

proposed_fixes.title: Match Git Bash shortcut rules to the mintty terminal process
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Keyboard Manager appears to match the configured git-bash.exe target against the wrong process identity; the interactive terminal runs in mintty.exe, which is not recognized as a child of the configured target.
plan: Trace process identity and parent/child resolution for a Keyboard Manager shortcut targeted to git-bash.exe while a Git Bash terminal is active.
Use the supported process relationship or an explicit terminal-process target resolution so the git-bash.exe rule applies to its mintty.exe terminal process.
Preserve exact app targeting and ensure unrelated mintty instances do not inherit the rule unless they belong to the configured Git Bash process.
Add regression coverage for Git Bash, direct mintty.exe targeting, and other child-process application targets.
verification: A Shift+A-to-B remap targeted to git-bash.exe sends lowercase b in its terminal.
A remap targeted directly to mintty.exe continues to work.
The mapping remains scoped to the intended application and does not affect unrelated terminals.

confidence.rationale: The current-build reproduction and mintty.exe workaround strongly isolate process targeting, but the precise process-resolution implementation and safe scope need code-level confirmation.

issue_context.summary: A shortcut remap targeted to git-bash.exe reportedly fails because the interactive mintty.exe terminal process is not recognized as its child.
known_information: The original report maps Shift+A to b for git-bash.exe and observes uppercase A instead.
The reporter says the mapping works in Chrome and when targeting All apps.
A commenter reproduced on PowerToys 0.100.2 and reports that targeting mintty.exe works.
The commenter identifies the unrecognized mintty.exe child relationship as the observed difference.
inferences: Process-target matching may need to resolve the Git Bash terminal child while keeping unrelated mintty processes outside the rule.
issue_context.analysis: The current-version reproduction and specific working alternative provide stronger evidence than the older closed issue #24954, which concerns different Esc/Caps Lock mappings in cmd. Keep the current mintty process-target observation as the primary evidence.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body and all three comments, including the current-build maintainer-style reproduction and mintty.exe workaround.
Reviewed closed issue #24954; it describes different key remaps in cmd and does not establish coverage for this Git Bash child-process target failure.

information_gaps.information: Whether the original reporter's mapping remains affected on current stable and whether targeting mintty.exe is an acceptable workaround for their configuration
information_gaps.why_needed: This confirms whether the original report is still active and whether the current-build reproduction matches the reporter's Git Bash setup.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm the current PowerToys and Git for Windows versions, repeat the mapping targeted to git-bash.exe, and compare with targeting mintty.exe.

actions.label: Reproduce Git Bash terminal process targeting

reproduce.title: Compare git-bash.exe and mintty.exe shortcut targets
prerequisites: Git for Windows with Git Bash installed
setup: Configure Shift+A to send b, first targeting git-bash.exe and then targeting mintty.exe.
steps: Open a Git Bash terminal and press Shift+A with the shortcut targeted to git-bash.exe.
Repeat with the same mapping targeted directly to mintty.exe.
Repeat in Chrome or another application to confirm the global mapping behavior is unchanged.
Open a separate mintty process, if available, and check whether it incorrectly inherits the Git Bash-specific rule.
reproduce.expected_result: The git-bash.exe-targeted shortcut applies in the Git Bash terminal, direct mintty.exe targeting remains functional, and unrelated applications or terminals are unaffected.

actions.label: Approve the Git Bash process-target fix
